t: You're looking at number 45 Pont Street, in the SW1X part of Kensington and Chelsea. It was designed by Charles William Stephens, known as C. W. Stephens, who lived from 1845 to 1917. Stephens was architect to the Harrods department store from 1892 until his death, and he's responsible for its famous Baroque-style façade on Brompton Road. His other London work includes the Harvey Nichols department store, the new Claridge's hotel, and the Park Lane Hotel. So this house comes from an architect who shaped some of the capital's best-known shops and hotels.
